_comment: STARTER SKETCH — nothing reads this yet. Role/economics annotations for
the mons whose value the leaf eval structurally cannot price.
WHY A DATA FILE AND NOT AN LLM CALL. The knowledge here is ENUMERABLE (a
few dozen meta mons, each with a stable role), so it belongs in a
versioned, diffable artifact with zero inference latency — the same call
made for ps_sets_overrides.json, where a 40-line overlay fixed the
Kingambit Low Kick blindness that would otherwise have needed a model.
An LLM+RAG pass over the smogon corpus is a good way to DRAFT this file
(Phase 0 of the overlay plan) but the artifact is the deliverable, and it
must be human-reviewed before anything consumes it. Contextual judgements
that cannot be enumerated ('is THIS Kingambit worth holding on THIS board')
stay with the search or a later live overlay.
WHY IT EXISTS AT ALL. Three open items are each blocked on the same
missing fact — which mons are cleaners, which are resource anchors, which
are meant to lead:
1. Kingambit hold-back annuity: the eval now prices Supreme Overlord's
fallen-ally scaling (poke-engine c68f15a) but still cannot see the
OPPORTUNITY COST of spending the cleaner early; it needs to know the
mon is a cleaner at all.
2. Weather preservation: measured 43% rain uptime with 41% of Swift Swim
moves clicked OUTSIDE rain — the search does not treat the setter's
survival as a resource, or the weather clock as a wasting asset.
3. Canonical-lead weighting: the preview matrix is nearly flat (row-min
spreads 0.01-0.12 at any depth) so lead choice is close to a coin
flip among near-ties; paste slot-1 and role are real human priors.
SAFETY CONTRACT: every consumer must degrade to current behaviour on a
missing entry. This file may only ADD information; it must never be
required. Absent species = today's engine, unchanged.
SCHEMA (per normalized species; `ability` qualifies when the role depends
on it, since the same species with another ability is a different mon):
tags         role labels, the primary key for consumers
ability      role holds only for this ability (omit = any)
value_curve  how worth changes over a game: flat | grows_with_own_faints
| decays_with_weather_clock | grows_with_hazards
preserve     how badly losing it costs beyond its own HP: low|med|high
resource     field state this mon CREATES; its death ends it
requires     field state this mon NEEDS to be worth its slot
lead_intent  human intent to lead it: avoid | neutral | strong
evidence     the measurement or commit this claim rests on
REVIEW RULE: an entry without `evidence` is a guess and should not ship.
Role tags are TESTABLE against behaviour — the Kingambit timing analysis
(first-entry turn, allies fallen at entry) is the template; a claimed
'cleaner' whose deployment timing does not move after wiring is a claim
that failed, not a fact.

kingambit.evidence: Supreme Overlord = +10% power per fallen ally (abilities.rs:2257), now mirrored into threat_vs (c68f15a). Timing instrument: we first deploy it ~T9 with 0.44 allies down and 77% of the time with ZERO down, vs the ladder population's T13.0 / 0.96. fp is equally guilty, so this is absolute strength, not fp-gap.

pelipper.evidence: rain_audit over 27 rain-team games: 43% average uptime where a piloted Damp Rock team lives 60-80%; uptime tracked outcomes (50% in wins vs 40% in losses). Rain teams benched at 29.2% board-only, the only below-pool-CI archetype.

barraskewda.evidence: 41% of Swift Swim moves across those games were clicked OUTSIDE rain (60 in / 42 out) — the search spends the abuser while its enabling condition is down.

torkoal.evidence: same audit: sun leaks identically (43% uptime) but sun teams win anyway (63%) because Protosynthesis abusers fall back on Booster Energy — so preserve pressure is genuinely LOWER here than for rain. Recorded to stop a future fix over-generalising 'weather setter' into one rule.

glimmora.evidence: RAG-grounded [smogon#Glimmora (gen9ou) — Lead]: the Lead set exists to deny setup — it stops "Ting-Lu from setting up entry hazards multiple times and Hatterene from trying to deny Stealth Rock with Magic Bounce". Confirms the suicide-lead role: its job is completed on the turns it survives, not by surviving. Directly relevant to richwoman, whose hazard stack is anchored by Ting-Lu (45 leads).

grimmsnarl.evidence: RAG-grounded [smogon#Grimmsnarl (gen9ou) — Dual Screens]: recommended set is Reflect / Light Screen / Taunt / Spirit Break with LIGHT CLAY, an item bought purely to extend the side conditions it leaves behind — the definition of expendable team-persistent support. Matches the monotype screens-setter precedent.

slowkinggalar.evidence: Regenerator pivots are net-positive on entry (fp routes hazard cycles through them: pays 12.5%, regains 33%) — the hazard_cycle finding. Also the mon whose speed floor produced the false Choice Scarf call (88f1f17), so its canonical spread is bulky with ~0 Speed.

gholdengo.evidence: richwoman's hazard-stack identity runs Gholdengo as the spinblock behind 3+ SR setters (11/23 of her games); its survival is what makes her chip mechanism work — the mirror of our own removal dependency.

gliscor.evidence: The flagship annuity case. Stall audit: fp's Poison Heal Gliscor played its FULL PP budget and generated 22.8 mons of free healing over three marathons while ours clicked 6 moves in ~711 turns. Eval terms shipped for exactly this (poke-engine 76af1e9: POISON_HEAL_STATUSED 15->35, PENDING +15) and our Gliscor now SubToxes at full budget. Known race: the naked orb walked into Knock Off on entry in 2/3 marathons, so activation timing is itself the play.

greattusk.evidence: MECHANIC certain (Rapid Spin), ECONOMICS unmeasured: hazard chip is our pinned loss mechanism (Stealth Rock = 21% of damage taken in richwoman's 42-turn grinds, ~7 switch-ins/game), so the only remover on a team is a team-persistent resource whose death re-exposes the whole side. `preserve: high` is CONDITIONAL on being the sole remover, which is a team property this per-species file cannot express — flagged as a schema gap, do not wire blindly. [RAG ATTEMPTED, NOT GROUNDED: a naive gen9ou-filtered query returned a topically-similar passage for the WRONG species (Deoxys-Speed and Zamazenta respectively) — retrieval needs a species filter, not just a format filter. Claim remains my inference.]

corviknight.evidence: RAG-grounded [smogon#Corviknight (gen9ou) — Defensive]: "Defog allows Corviknight to fulfill the role as the team's hazard remover", and Pressure "more quickly stall[s] out their attacks' PP" against setup sweepers (Dragonite, Gliscor, Kingambit). Sole-remover caveat still applies: preserve pressure is a TEAM property this per-species file cannot express. PP-stalling matters in the long grinds where the stall audit measured real PP bankruptcy.

rillaboom.evidence: RAG-grounded [smogon#Rillaboom (gen9ou) — Utility]: Grassy Terrain is described as "solving its problem with longevity" for partners and enabling Grassy-Seed setup — i.e. the terrain is a TEAM-WIDE annuity (passive recovery + halved Earthquake), not a personal buff, so the setter's death ends a resource the whole side was drawing on. Same economics shape as the weather setters; RE-RUN the rain_audit for terrain before assigning preserve pressure, since sun leaked identically to rain and did not care.

walkingwake.evidence: Hydro Steam is sun-boosted rather than sun-nerfed, and Protosynthesis falls back on Booster Energy when the sun drops — which is exactly WHY sun tolerates engine piloting (63%) while rain does not (29.2%, benched). Recorded to keep the weather fix from treating all abusers as equally weather-dependent.

dragonite.evidence: MECHANIC certain (Multiscale halves damage at FULL HP only, already modelled in damage_calc). ECONOMICS: its defensive half is a one-shot resource that any chip destroys — the same Stealth-Rock tax that drives our loss mechanism deletes it on a single switch-in, which is why the standard set runs Boots. The eval prices Multiscale when at full HP but cannot price PRESERVING full HP for a later sweep. [RAG ATTEMPTED, NOT GROUNDED: a naive gen9ou-filtered query returned a topically-similar passage for the WRONG species (Deoxys-Speed and Zamazenta respectively) — retrieval needs a species filter, not just a format filter. Claim remains my inference.]

ceruledge.evidence: RAG-CORRECTED [smogon#Ceruledge (gen9ou) — Swords Dance]: my inference said Focus Sash is a resource chip destroys, i.e. preserve it. The analysis says the opposite — hitting Ceruledge with weak moves "to pop the item would only give it a trouble-free Weak Armor boost", so LOSING the Sash is frequently net-positive because Weak Armor triggers on being hit. Sash is insurance for the setup turn, not a resource to protect. preserve lowered to 'low'; the naive 'one-shot item = preserve' generalisation from Multiscale does NOT transfer here.

ironmoth.evidence: RAG-grounded [smogon#Iron Moth (gen9ou) — Booster Energy]: the recommended set is Booster Energy with Fiery Dance / Sludge Wave / coverage / Substitute, i.e. the item is spent on entry BY DESIGN to switch on Quark Drive. Consistent with the item-polarity finding (consumption is the point, not a loss). Remaining unpriced question is TIMING — which entry spends it — which the eval does not model.

tinglu.evidence: richwoman's most-used lead by a distance (45 of her games) and the anchor of the hazard-stack that produces our pinned chip loss. Her revealed set is SR/Whirlwind/Earthquake/Ruination — Whirlwind is what converts her hazards into forced-switch chip.

deoxysspeed.evidence: RAG-grounded [smogon#Deoxys-Speed (gen9ou) — Hazard Lead]: "Focus Sash guarantees it can set at least one layer of entry hazard against faster threats... or even set two layers against slower threats" — the set is explicitly built to trade itself for hazards, confirming the suicide-lead role rather than a mon to preserve.

pecharunt.evidence: CORRECTION 2026-07-31 (user-flagged, verified): Poison Puppeteer IS implemented — generate_instructions.rs:907 adds CONFUSION to a foe it poisons, landed in 2e000e6 alongside Rock Head/Anger Shell/Synchronize. An earlier memory note listing it as a silent OU gap was stale. The engine models it correctly; this is now an ordinary role entry.
